cites.quote: The patient list has a column titled `Last visit`.
The Last visit date is the appointment's date in the hospital time zone, `Asia/Kolkata`.
Completed appointment is the Completed appointment with the latest `start time`.
A patient with no Completed appointment shows `\"-\"` in the Last visit column.
The patient list stays at `20 per page`.
Blood group, allergies, chronic conditions, current medications and notes of one patient.
Given a patient with two Completed appointments, when the patient list is shown, then Last visit shows the date of the one with the latest start time (assumed REQ-4).
The ticket does not say which timestamp orders appointments

findings.suggested_fix: Set up the test so the appointment with the later start time was closed (marked Completed) before the earlier one. Then only start-time ordering passes.
findings.text: S-1 AC3 does not test the assumed REQ-4 ordering. With two Completed appointments, ordering by start time, closing time or creation time usually gives the same answer, so the test passes whichever key the code uses.

cites.quote: falls on a different calendar date in Asia/Kolkata than in the server's time zone

findings.suggested_fix: Describe the setup with a fixed instant instead, for example a Completed appointment starting at 20:00 UTC, which is the next calendar date in Asia/Kolkata, and expect the Asia/Kolkata date.
findings.text: S-1 AC4 depends on the server time zone, which neither the intent nor the AC fixes. If the server already runs in Asia/Kolkata, this setup cannot be built and the time-zone conversion goes untested.

cites.quote: Given more than 20 patients, when staff open the patient list, then each page shows 20 patients.
- AC1: Each page still shows 20 patients.

findings.suggested_fix: Copy the front-matter criteria into the body word for word so the two do not drift apart.
findings.text: The body criteria for S-2 and S-3 are shortened, not in Given/When/Then form, and drop preconditions from the front matter. For example, S-3 AC1 in the body leaves out 'Given more than 20 patients'.

rubric_items.reason: All 13 REQs from the intent are traced. REQ-1 to REQ-4 go to S-1, REQ-5 to REQ-8 to S-2, REQ-9 to REQ-12 to S-3 and REQ-13 to S-4. The assumed REQ-4 is flagged in S-1.
Each story has one outcome. S-3 groups four separate no-regression checks (paging, search, sort, Next appointment). That is acceptable as one outcome, but it is a broad story.

The front-matter criteria all use Given/When/Then and can be checked. S-1 AC3 cannot tell start-time ordering apart from other orderings. S-1 AC4 only works if the server time zone differs from Asia/Kolkata.
Every value in the criteria comes from the intent: 'Last visit', '-', 20 per page, Asia/Kolkata, the status names and the medical-history fields.
Easy to read, and the terms match the intent. The body criteria are shortened, not in Given/When/Then form, and differ from the front-matter versions.
